page: Microsoft Azure A4m_v2 is an Av2-family memory-intensive virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The server is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, backed by a Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Cache specifications include 32 KB L1d, 0.25 MB L2, and 50 MB L3 cache. The CPU supports AVX, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA instructions, but lacks AVX-512 capabilities. Local storage is limited to a bundled 41 GB volume, and there are no integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the A4m_v2 operates in the bottom 10% across all evaluated performance metrics. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU benchmarks recorded scores of 350.4 and 1343.8, respectively. Memory performance is constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth at 12.77 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 10.01 GB/sec, though small-block cached reads reach 123.33 GB/sec. Geekbench testing yielded a single-core score of 336.0 and a multi-core score of 1106.0. Redis SET operations achieved 1.84 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reached 1.45 GB/sec. These results highlight a significant performance tradeoff, where memory capacity is prioritized over processing speed and throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the A4m_v2 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio on older-generation hardware, making it a budget-friendly option for workloads requiring larger memory footprints without demanding high CPU performance. It is appropriate for lightweight database hosting, basic memory-cached applications, development environments, and low-traffic web serving. It is not recommended for compute-intensive tasks, large-scale data processing, or modern machine learning workloads due to its low processing benchmarks and lack of GPU acceleration.
